summary: Figure F6_risk_utility illustrates the trade-off between utility (U) and risk (R_bar) for different defense variants in a theoretical framework. The goal is to minimize risk while maintaining a certain level of utility, as defined by the constraint $U_\tau \geq U_{none} - \eta$. The none variant has the highest utility but also the highest risk, while some variants like datamark_dynamic show a significant reduction in risk at the cost of lower utility.
observations: The none variant has the highest utility (U = 1.00) and the highest risk (R_bar = 1.00).
The datamark_dynamic variant has the lowest utility (U = 0.96) but the lowest risk (R_bar = 0.37768).
The random_scramble variant has the lowest utility (U = 0.50) and the lowest risk (R_bar = 0.21642).
The base64 variant has a moderate utility (U = 0.75) and a high risk (R_bar = 1.00).
caveats: The data is in theory-mode and simulated, so the results are not based on real-world experiments.
The sample size is small (11 rows), which may limit the generalizability of the findings.
The figure does not provide information on the actual performance metrics or real-world applicability of the defense variants.
